analysis.title: Inside Commodities, November 6, 2026
key_insights: Middle East crude spot premiums fell back to pre-war levels. Dubai's cash premium to swaps hit 65 cents a barrel on Monday, the lowest since July, and recovered to $1.55 on Thursday. Oman dropped to 95 cents on Tuesday and was $1.76 on Thursday. Last month's average premium was about $8 a barrel.

The premium drop was driven by unsold December-loading Oman, Murban and Iraqi cargoes, plus weaker Asian refining margins. J.P.Morgan analysts say higher September and October Gulf exports created a surplus, even with rising attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.

Kpler says UAE Murban exports hit a record 2.4 million bpd in September and eased to about 2 million bpd in October, against 1.2-1.5 million bpd in January-February. UAE output rose above 3.9 million bpd in September versus a pre-war 3.4 million bpd.

Kpler revised up its Saudi, Iraq and Kuwait production figures on more loadings and inventory depletion. Middle East crude flows, including bypass pipelines, averaged 17.1 million bpd in September and 16.3 million bpd in October. Iraqi flows reached 3.35 million bpd in October, 150,000 bpd below pre-war levels.

West African and Brazilian sellers are offering steeper discounts to Chinese buyers to offset high freight, competing with Gulf grades. Shandong independent refiners bought 8-10 million barrels of November-loading West African crude last week.

Asian refiners are unlikely to raise crude purchases until margins improve. China's larger-than-expected fourth batch of fuel export quotas raised expectations of more Asian supply and weighed on margins. Gasoline margins are at their lowest since late February. 10-ppm sulphur diesel margins are slightly above $60 a barrel, down from a record above $87 in mid-September.

J.P.Morgan estimates the global oil market returned to a 1.1 million bpd surplus in September and a 1.4 million bpd surplus in October, close to last year's 1.3 million bpd average. Global crude imports in October were above the 2025 average while demand lags. Banks and government forecasters have cut 2026 demand forecasts partly because of high prices.

Goldman Sachs estimates global oil stocks did not fall in September-October after falling sizeably in the months after the war began. It sees the market as broadly balanced in that period, against a deficit in March. A marginal surplus carried from last year, higher non-Gulf output and weaker demand helped balance it.

Vortexa says Gulf crude and condensate exports averaged 14 million bpd in October, about 86% of pre-war levels, and refined product exports averaged 3.1 million bpd, just over half of normal. October crude shipments edged below September's post-war high, and two ship-tracking firms said October could be revised up.

Brent market structure gives mixed signals. Prompt Brent swaps (contracts for differences) are in contango, with this week's contract at the steepest discount to next week's since July, which points to ample prompt physical supply. Brent futures from January 2027 delivery remain in backwardation, which points to tight near-term supply. Trader Adi Imsirovic says futures could move to contango if swaps stay there, since such shifts usually start in the physical market.

China's commerce ministry says it will buy more US farm goods only if the sides implement the agreed reciprocal tariff-cut arrangement. The proposed package is $60 billion of reciprocal tariff cuts, including about $17 billion of US farm goods China imported in 2024, and is not finalised.

China is on track to meet its soybean purchase target but bought only $7.2 billion of other US farm products from January to September, per a Reuters analysis. Non-soy imports are the lowest for the period since 2019. It is unclear when the clock starts on the $17 billion non-soy deal. An agricultural working group is expected to meet before year-end, and traders say lower tariffs are needed to make large purchases commercially viable.

The USDA attache in Beijing sees China's 2026-27 soybean imports at 110 million tons, below the USDA's official 115 million. China has committed to at least 25 MMT of US soybeans for MY 26/27 and had bought 15.1 MMT as of October 22, with 5.9 MMT of US exports to China so far. A 10% retaliatory tariff leads commercial buyers to South American suppliers. Chinese soybean oil exports are projected at a record 1.35 MMT.

Morocco paused tomato exports to African markets to lower domestic prices after lower output in Souss Massa and higher fertiliser and fuel costs. Exports to Europe are exempt. The government calls the halt temporary. Morocco is the second-largest tomato exporter to the EU.

Lula's re-election in Brazil makes fast US access to Brazil's rare earths less likely. The new CIMCE council will prioritise domestic processing and set new rules for investment incentives and priority projects, with regulations expected in the first few months of 2027. It claims 27 minerals, with rare earths classed as high priority. Only the Serra Verde mine, bought by USA Rare Earth in September, is commercially operating, and it is not expected at full capacity until the end of next year.

Chinese copper smelters face a squeeze as sulphuric acid prices fall. Acid had offset losses from negative treatment and refining charges. Chinese acid prices are about 1,484 yuan per ton versus a July peak of 2,107 yuan. Spot copper treatment charges hit a record low of minus $246.40 a ton on October 30. Jiangxi Copper and Yunnan Copper reported sharp Q3 profit declines from Q2, and some smelters have extended maintenance outages. Output is on track for its slowest pace in decades, and sources say production cuts are coming.

The IEA expects emerging and developing economies outside China to add about as much renewable capacity as advanced economies over 2026-2031 for the first time. Global additions are forecast at almost 4,800 GW, with about 1,100 GW from emerging and developing economies, 2,550 GW from China and China's share falling to 53% by 2031 from 60% in 2025. Grid connection delays are a constraint, and the IEA raised its biofuels forecast by 40%.

China's Q3 CO2 emissions from energy and industry fell 3.1% y/y, the biggest quarterly drop since the pandemic, per CREA. China's oil use fell 4% and transport oil use fell 9%. Coal use fell 3.3%. Emissions are down 0.5% in the first three quarters.

Ukraine's grain rail shipments for export rose 26% m/m to 1.08 million tons in October. Seaports, which handled 90% of grain exports, have been effectively blocked since late July by Russian attacks, so shipments run through Danube ports and western land borders. Danube capacity is capped at about 500,000 tons a month and rail attacks are rising.
earnings_insights: Jiangxi Copper and Yunnan Copper reported sharp declines in Q3 profit versus Q2, per Reuters calculations from company filings. No EPS or revenue figures are given.

macro_indicators.reading: surplus of 1.1 million bpd in September, 1.4 million bpd in October
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supply recovery and weak demand have returned the market to surplus. The October surplus nearly matches last year's average of 1.3 million bpd.

macro_indicators.indicator: Global oil market balance (Goldman Sachs estimate)
macro_indicators.reading: broadly balanced, versus a deficit in March
macro_indicators.interpretation: Global stocks did not decline over the two months after falling sizeably early in the war.

macro_indicators.reading: 65 cents a barrel Monday low, $1.55 Thursday
macro_indicators.interpretation: The premium fell from an October average of about $8, which signals ample prompt Gulf supply.

macro_indicators.reading: 17.1 million bpd September, 16.3 million bpd October
macro_indicators.interpretation: Flows including bypass pipelines are recovering, with September the highest since the war started.
More Chinese product supply in Asia weighs on regional refining margins.

macro_indicators.indicator: China CO2 emissions from energy and industry
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower oil and coal use reflects the Hormuz crisis, EV adoption, mild weather and better wind and solar use.
Below the USDA's official 115 million ton projection, which is a smaller call on US and global soybean demand.
A record low means smelters are paying for ore, which squeezes margins and supports output cuts.

risk_factors: Rising attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
No resolution to the Iran war, with a risk of renewed export disruption.
October Gulf export figures could be revised up, which would add to the supply picture.
US-China tariff-cut deal not finalised, with uncertainty over when the $17 billion non-soy purchase clock starts.
Chinese copper smelter losses and output cuts, with Panmure Liberum's Tom Price expecting more acid price downside if the US-Iran war ends.
Grid connection delays slowing renewable additions.
Danube port capacity limits, weather and rail attacks constraining Ukrainian grain exports.
vol_and_positioning: Brent swaps (contracts for differences) show contango at the steepest prompt discount since July. Brent futures from January 2027 remain in backwardation. Imsirovic says futures could shift to contango if swaps stay there.
geopolitical: US-Israeli war with Iran, which began in late February 2026, with no resolution. An initial agreement in July to end the war allowed more Gulf exports through the Strait of Hormuz, but attacks on vessels transiting the strait are rising.
US-China trade: the September Xi-Trump summit in Washington proposed a $60 billion reciprocal tariff-cut package that is not finalised. China ties US farm purchases to its implementation.
China's 10% retaliatory tariff on US soybeans remains, and Chinese state-owned enterprises buy US soybeans under the Busan agreement.
Brazil: Lula's re-election over Flavio Bolsonaro reduces US prospects for preferential rare earth access. Brazil prioritises local processing through the new CIMCE council.
Russia-Ukraine: Russian attacks have effectively blocked Ukrainian seaports since late July and attacks on rail are rising.
Morocco paused tomato exports to African markets on domestic food price concerns.
cross_bank_references: J.P.Morgan sees a 1.1 million bpd global oil surplus in September and 1.4 million bpd in October, while Goldman Sachs sees the market broadly balanced over September-October.

tension_points.bull_case: Brent futures from January 2027 delivery remain in backwardation, which indicates near-term supply is still tight. Goldman sees the market broadly balanced, with stocks not falling in September-October.
tension_points.bear_case: Prompt Brent swaps are in contango at the steepest discount since July, which signals ample immediate supply. J.P.Morgan estimates a 1.4 million bpd October surplus and Middle East premiums have returned to pre-war levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Brent futures moving into contango while prompt swaps stay in contango would confirm the surplus read and break the tight-supply read.

theme_stances.key_argument: Recovering Middle East flows, rising non-Gulf output and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption.
theme_stances.evidence: returned to a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day in September

theme_stances.key_argument: Falling acid prices remove the byproduct profit that offset negative treatment charges, and production cuts are coming.
